latest.summary: OpenAI has reorganised its Model Spec, the public rulebook for its AI, around five values led by faithfulness to human intent. It adds guidance on context and human agency, drops most style rules and ...
highlights: OpenAI has reorganised its Model Spec, the public rulebook for its AI, around five values led by faithfulness to human intent. It adds guidance on context and human agency, drops most style rules and renames the model GPT. OpenAI admits its models do not yet fully follow it. OpenAI has rewritten its Model Spec, the public rulebook for how its AI should behave, around five core values, the company said on Thursday. The update also drops most of its style rules and now calls the model “GPT” rather than “the assistant.”. OpenAI calls faithfulness the foundation: the model should grasp what people actually want rather than follow instructions word for word. The model should also not tell people what it thinks they want to hear. OpenAI admits its models “do not yet fully reflect” the Spec and says it is testing new training methods to teach the values.

latest.title: Claude Model Builds Exploits Across Major Browsers & OSes - Dark Reading
latest.summary: # Claude Model Builds Exploits Across Major Browsers & OSes. An unreleased version of the AI model has found and chained multiple vulnerabilities in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux, Anthro...
highlights: # Claude Model Builds Exploits Across Major Browsers & OSes. An unreleased version of the AI model has found and chained multiple vulnerabilities in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux, Anthropic says. An unreleased version of Claude identified critical vulnerabilities in some of the world's most widely used browsers and operating systems and chained them into working exploits requiring little or no human interaction, Anthropic said this week. The exploits included one that enabled data theft from a locked Android smartphone, another zero-click exploit allowed remote code execution (RCE) with root privileges on Linux servers, and a third that could have allowed attackers to remotely crash Windows systems. In total, Anthropic said, the model generated five working exploits targeting Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux. Each of the vulnerabilities that Claude discovered helped overcome a different security control and allowed the chained exploit to escape the browser's sandbox.

In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space:. highlights: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. The release comes as competition between open-weight AI developers like Mistral and closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic heats up, with the former arguing that businesses and governments shouldn’t have to rely on outside AI companies for access to advanced capabilities. Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.”. The release of the model’s weights — the numerical training that animates the system — ensures that other companies and government agencies will now be able to deploy ML4 for their own purposes.

highlights: ## A small red team with frontier AI can now out-find a much bigger traditional one, so the winners will be operators who pair smart judgment with smart tools. It’s that the economics of attack changed entirely — and those of us who run red teams have had a front-row seat to the transformation. A small, well-equipped offensive team using frontier AI models today can outperform what was possible with a much larger traditional operation just two years ago, by a margin that should unsettle every security leader reading this. Through our work on the front lines of offensive security, the consensus is clear: if you are not augmenting your operations with AI, you are already at a disadvantage. * **Red teaming *with* AI:** Using AI as an operator’s tool to execute traditional offensive operations. It is this second category, Red Teaming *with* AI, where the most immediate, drastic, and dangerous transformation is occurring.

latest.title: AI Is Destroying Academic Publishing - The Atlantic
latest.summary: # AI Is Destroying Academic Publishing. As a journal editor, I can say: The currency of academic social capital is collapsing. Weak scholarship was once easy to spot at a glance: The signs included ba...
highlights: # AI Is Destroying Academic Publishing. As a journal editor, I can say: The currency of academic social capital is collapsing. Weak scholarship was once easy to spot at a glance: The signs included bad writing, a lack of relevant citations, and little engagement with previous scholarship, such as a paper that promised a “novel” conceptual framework without acknowledging the many other papers making similar claims. As an associate editor of a bioethics journal, I’d make a quick “desk reject” decision and not send these articles for peer review, which effectively killed any hope of publication. Now I can say: AI is affecting every part of academic publishing. There are sentences that have all of the trappings of real arguments, but that rarely make sense—such as “Algorithmic triage functions less as a clinical tool than as an infrastructure of deferred accountability.” There are citations that refer only to open-access or highly cited articles, because the most popular LLMs can’t readily access paywalled journal articles, so they rely on what’s either free or described at length elsewhere.

highlights: OpenAI is saying it has no plans to go public this year – but senior Wall Street executives say they fully expect it will happen in the first quarter of 2027, On The Money has learned. The artificial intelligence giant run by Sam Altman has been quick to shoot down rumors that it’s preparing to IPO imminently now that archrival Anthropic has filed its S-1 as a precursor to a deal that’s expected in late November. Altman has been among the AI industry’s top alarmists – as has Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei – although that isn’t stopping the latter from cashing in on an initial public offering that could value the company as high as $2 trillion, possibly even surpassing SpaceX’s record-breaking IPO. Meanwhile, finance bigs are warning Altman that his iPO window could be closing with rising fears of an AI bubble and competition for investor capital – not just from the Anthropic sale but also a planned massive secondary stock sale by Meta, as first reported by On The Money.

On CWE-bench, which measures patching, it scored 71.0%. On Google’s internal tests, Carbon was more than twice as successful as Argon at writing secure code. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Carbon’s rate of successful cheating was 0.0%. GPT-6 Astra leads on FrontierSWE 2, a software engineering test, with 65.5% against Carbon’s 61.2%. > “With Gemini 4 Argon and now Carbon, which we announced today, we’re excited to be leading at the frontier,” Pichai said.
